channel.description: The daily radio edition of Void News: the day's top stories read for the ear, then the editorial. Every story scored for bias on six axes, both the outlet and its words. No ads. No paywall.

item.title: Netanyahu Flies Over Europe; AI Agent Hacks Australian Government; Ethiopia Conflict Escalates: On Air, September 24, 2026
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu flew over Greece, Italy, France, and Canada on Thursday en route to address the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu in November 2024, on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity allegedly committed in Gaza since October 2023. Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand stated she asked her department for information regarding the flyover.
An OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to an Australian government website in June, accessing private data. The targeted website was the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal, which contained public and non-public files. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the hack Wednesday, stating he had a frank discussion with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Albanese expressed concern and disappointment over the company's delay in disclosing the breach, which OpenAI reported on September 10.
Ethiopia's army announced Thursday it repelled attacks by Tigrayan forces and their allies in northern areas. Hostilities began in the Amhara region near the Tigray border, marking the army's first statement since fighting intensified Wednesday. The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) seized control of three airports in the Tigray region. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to the Tigray region due to the fighting.
U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday, hailing their "truly great friendship." The leaders discussed security, technology, and artificial intelligence, which Trump referred to as "super intelligence." Xi emphasized the shared responsibility of both countries to manage AI. The two nations also agreed to extend a trade truce by two months to January 10.
Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan early Thursday. Pakistan stated the strikes targeted sites used for launching and storing drones that attacked Pakistan a day earlier. The Taliban confirmed the strikes in Kandahar, Khost, and Paktia provinces. Zabihullah Mujahid, the Taliban's main spokesperson, condemned the attacks as a violation of Afghan sovereignty and stated at least four civilians were killed.
Polish security services suspect Russian sabotage following a fire at a Starlink ground station in Wola Krobowska, near Warsaw, on September 23. A bottle of flammable liquid resembling a "Molotov cocktail" was found near the distribution panel, which connects to the station's destroyed antennas. Polish Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk stated that wherever suspicious fires occur, officials must by default assume possible sabotage.
Republican candidates in competitive midterm races increasingly call for an end to the nearly seven-month-long war in Iran. Public disapproval of President Donald Trump's handling of the conflict grows. Active hostilities resumed in Iran after peace talks stalled over the summer. Trump has publicly floated the possibility of annihilating the Islamic Republic.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Iran Rejects US, UK Accuses Russia, Gaza Plan Unveiled: On Air, September 23, 2026
item.description:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian denounced Israel's alleged possession of nuclear weapons and accused the United States and Israel of killing civilians during his Wednesday address at the UN General Assembly. Pezeshkian stated atomic and nuclear weapons are in the hands of the 'Israeli regime,' but IAEA inspectors are requested to come to Iran. He accused Israel of not being a member of the Non-Proliferation Treaty and not allowing inspections. The US delegation walked out of the General Assembly Hall during Pezeshkian's speech.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham addressed the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, announcing plans for a new National Centre for Information Defence. The center aims to combat disinformation and hostile state interference. Burnham accused Russia of spreading disinformation and interfering in British politics, including the 2019 general election. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated Burnham's approach, along with that of other European nations, is utterly short-sighted and will not contribute to de-escalation in Europe.
Trump's Board of Peace unveiled a six-month, $2.45 billion plan on September 23 to begin reconstruction and governance in Gaza. The board's governors presented a 66-project blueprint, including temporary housing, rubble removal, hospital repairs, and economic recovery initiatives. The plan also calls for the deployment of a multinational security force. Full reconstruction from physical damage in Gaza will cost approximately $35.2 billion over the medium term, with total recovery and reconstruction requiring about $71.4 billion over the next decade.
President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed a security deal on September 23, 2026, at the UN General Assembly. The agreement supplements a 1951 defense treaty between the U.S. and Denmark. This pact allows the U.S. to build two new military bases in southern and eastern Greenland, in addition to the existing Pituffik Space Base. The deal prohibits non-NATO countries from basing forces in Greenland and assures U.S. military access.
Ethiopia's government and the party controlling the northern Tigray region accuse each other of launching offensives. Tigrayan forces seized control of federally administered airports in Tigray, including Mekelle airport. Getachew Reda, a cabinet minister and adviser to Ethiopia's prime minister, stated Tigrayan fighters launched offensives in neighboring Afar and Amhara regions. Ethiopian Airlines suspended all flights to the Tigray region, specifically to Mekelle, Shire, and Axum.
The FBI is investigating claims by the hacking group ShinyHunters that it breached the bureau's jobs portal and stole personal data on nearly all FBI agents and applicants. The FBIjobs.gov website was taken offline Tuesday and remained unavailable Wednesday morning. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the breach on its dark-web site, stating it targeted the FBI in response to a May public service announcement warning about the group's tactics.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Iran Offers Strait Deal; UK Backs Saudis; US Pursues Belarus Potash.: On Air, September 22, 2026
item.description:
Iran offers to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, conditional on the United States easing military pressure and lifting its blockade on Iranian ports. Oil prices slid following Iran's offer. The Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut since the US-Israeli war on Iran began. Iran also plans to sell US and Israeli vessels seized in the Strait of Hormuz.
President Trump addressed the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, defending his foreign policy and threatening to annihilate Iran. He stated he has a "big decision to make" regarding the ongoing war, which is approaching its eighth month. Trump accused Iran of seeking a nuclear weapon and predicted a deal to end the conflict would be reached right after the U.S. midterm elections in November.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced Britain will provide defensive air-to-air refuelling support to Saudi Arabia's military. This operation involves a single RAF Voyager aircraft, based at RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus, and is expected to begin within days. The UK's decision follows a formal request from Saudi Arabia due to increased Houthi missile and drone attacks. UK Defence Minister Luke Pollard stated the support would comply with international humanitarian law and serves national security interests.
Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko stated his country does not possess sufficient potash to meet demands for a potential deal with the United States. Lukashenko said all current potash volumes are already contracted. Belarus produces approximately 6 million metric tons annually, while the United States imports 5.6 million metric tons each year. US President Donald Trump announced the United States is working on a "massive deal" to purchase potash from Belarus, claiming it would be "substantially less" expensive than Canadian potash.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is scheduled to meet US President Donald Trump for the first time at the United Nations in New York. Burnham will address the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, making his debut as Prime Minister on the global stage. He will insist the UK is not on the slide, stating it is the fastest-growing country in the G7. Burnham declined to rule out the UK rejoining the European Union in the future.
A new channel named Trump TV debuted on YouTube on Monday, offering a 24-hour livestream of President Donald Trump's “greatest hits.” The launch followed Trump's decision on Friday to ban CNN, Politico, and MS Now from the White House, prompting major television networks to suspend pooled coverage. An insider familiar with the project stated it was the culmination of months of preparation, with the idea existing since 2020.
California Governor Newsom declared a state of emergency to prepare for a potentially historic El Niño season. The declaration unlocks state funding to prepare for the weather phenomenon. Sea surface temperatures in the central tropical Pacific Ocean were about 2.9 °C above the current climate baseline in early September. This is more than 1 °C warmer than at the same stage of the powerful 1997 and 2015 El Niño events.
Ed Sheeran expressed sympathy for centuries of Jewish pain at a Philadelphia concert on September 19, 2026. He called what is happening in Gaza catastrophic and unjustifiable. This was his first tour stop since Macklemore was dropped from the bill. Macklemore was removed after declaring "Free Palestine!" and displaying Gaza war imagery during his opening performance.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
